svg.text: Collaborative editing (Google Docs): concurrent edits must converge without locking anyone out
The problem: positions shift
doc = "ABC" Alice: insert("X", 1) Bob: delete(2) (meant to delete "C")
Apply Alice first → "AXBC"; Bob's delete(2) now removes "B", not "C". Same ops, different order → different documents.
Two people deleting the same char twice → two chars gone. Ops are neither commutative nor idempotent.
Operational Transformation (OT)
client ops
central server
orders + transforms
Bob's delete(2) transformed
against insert(1) → delete(3) ✔
+ index-based, small ops, what Google Docs uses
− needs a central ordering server
− transform functions are notoriously hard to get right
CRDT
every character gets a unique ID + a position between neighbours
insert X → X(1.5) (nobody else moves)
delete → delete id of "C", not index 2
+ ops commute and are idempotent → any order converges
+ works offline / peer-to-peer
− per-character metadata, tombstones grow, needs compaction
Around the algorithm: WebSocket per editor · op queue batches tiny edits before writing · edit history in an append-only / time-series
store (version restore = replay/diff) · presence + cursors via pub-sub · comments in a separate store · locks are wrong here:
they block everyone typing in the same paragraph.
